'''Michael G. Eastwood''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|FAA}} is a mathematician at the [[University of Adelaide]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=School of Mathematical Sciences|url=http://www.maths.adelaide.edu.au/people/michael.eastwood|access-date=2020-06-29|website=www.maths.adelaide.edu.au}}</ref> known for his work in [[twistor theory]], conformal differential geometry and invariant differential operators. In 1976<ref>{{Cite web|title=Robert C. Gunning's webpage|url=https://web.math.princeton.edu/~gunning/}}</ref> he received a PhD at [[Princeton University]] in [[several complex variables]] under [[Robert C. Gunning]]. He was a member of the twistor research group of [[Roger Penrose]] at the [[University of Oxford]] and he coauthored the monograph ''The Penrose Transform: Its Interaction with Representation Theory'' with Robert Baston.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bailey|first=T. N.|title=R. J. Baston and M. G. Eastwood, The Penrose transform: its interaction with representation theory (Oxford Mathematical Monographs, Clarendon Press, Oxford1989), pp. 232, 019 853565 1, £25.|journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society|year=1991|language=en|volume=34|issue=3|pages=497–498|doi=10.1017/S0013091500005265|issn=1464-3839|doi-access=free}}</ref> After moving to South Australia in 1985 he was the 1992 recipient of the [[Australian Mathematical Society Medal]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aust MS : The Australian Mathematical Society Medal|url=https://austms.org.au/awards-grants/awards/the-australian-mathematical-society-medal/|access-date=2020-08-28|website=www.austms.org.au}}</ref> and made a [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michael Eastwood|url=https://www.science.org.au/profile/michael-eastwood|access-date=2020-06-29|website=www.science.org.au|language=en}}</ref> In 2012 he was named to the inaugural (2013) class of fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2013|title=2013 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2020-11-02}}</ref>
